analysis: Only scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py changed, and it is a CI test script. The visible hunks mark build-cluster, build-provider and cluster-release-checks as not `required` in PLAN_LANES (head lines ~107-109). While job sizes are off, these lanes now ask the plane without a size (UNSIZED_PLAN_REQUEST extended at head 118-121, assertions adjusted around 600-622 and 684-699). The test still pins the safety properties: routing is on only when the switch is exactly `on`; fork PRs never contact the plane; the router accepts only exact label arrays per profile; HTTPS and certificate verification are enforced; plane text cannot inject workflow commands or markdown; release and credentialed workflows keep literal Blacksmith runners (UNROUTED); and routed jobs have read-only permissions, no secrets and bounded timeouts. The base text shows the test asserting that the three build and release-check lanes keep Blacksmith when sizes are off. The head now lets them take the unsized Darkbloom labels (self-hosted macOS). The test change only reflects a workflow change that is not in this batch (provider-plan.yml and provider-tests.yml, not supplied). Whether build-cluster, build-provider and cluster-release-checks produce artifacts that feed release or signing paths is unverified. The UNROUTED tests cover release-swift, release-provider and the other release workflows. That is a CI trust-boundary question, not a provider-threat-model asset. Nothing here touches the threat-model assets (A-001..A-020), the provider code, attestation, the cache or the coordinator. No security regression is evident in the supplied test code. Remaining question for integration: confirm in provider-plan.yml that routing build lanes to self-hosted Darkbloom runners with unsized labels does not feed a release or signing pipeline. The test's CI_ROUTED and UNROUTED sets suggest it does not.
